The most common win left on "MAX-A-MILLION" is $30. The second biggest prize left is $100,000, and six of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

The table below shows the full count for "MAX-A-MILLION", with every prize level included.
985.headline: A close look at the prizes

988.body:
The most common win left on "Emerald 10's" is $10. The second biggest prize left is $50,000, and three of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

The numbers for "Emerald 10's" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
988.headline: What's actually left to win

990.body:
The top prize count on "LADY LUCK" has not moved since we started watching it. The game still has two of four top prizes unclaimed. Smaller prizes keep getting claimed as tickets sell. The same top prizes are now among fewer tickets.

The numbers for "LADY LUCK" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
990.headline: Top prizes are still unclaimed

992.body:
"$2 MILLION VAULT" has one of three top prizes left and is well into its run. About three-quarters of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, the top prizes are being claimed more slowly than the tickets are selling, which is a good sign.

Today's free summary of "$2 MILLION VAULT" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
992.headline: How far along this game is

993.body:
"$5,000 Triple Play" has had no $5,000 top prize claimed for four months. Everyday prizes keep getting claimed, and fewer tickets are left each day. The number of tickets printed is fixed. Each day without a top prize claim leaves those prizes among fewer tickets.

Every line of $5,000 Triple Play's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
993.headline: Top prizes have lasted so far

994.body:
"$25,000 Triple Play" is past the halfway point of its run, with about a quarter of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, tickets and top prizes are running out at about the same rate.

Tomorrow's count on "$25,000 Triple Play" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
994.headline: Where this game is in its run

995.body:
"$200,000 Triple Play" has 176,728 prizes of $10 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $5,000 prize, with two left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

Tomorrow's count on "$200,000 Triple Play" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
995.headline: What the prize table shows

996.body:
"$1,000,000 Triple Play" has four of five top prizes left and is past the halfway point of its run. About two-thirds of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, tickets are selling faster than top prizes are being claimed, which is good for the tickets that are left.

The numbers for "$1,000,000 Triple Play" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
